records.text: The group were not sure whether to include a base/recharger for the remote.
The Project Manager then began a discussion to decide what was going into the final design.
The group had to change many of the original design elements to an alternative.
Several of the features that the group had wanted to integrate into the design were either too costly or unavailable due to new limitations from the factory.
He suggested they should focus on either expert or novice users.
The project manager opened the meeting and stated the agenda to the team members.
The team then discussed various features to consider in making the remote.
The user interface designer will work on the technical functions of the remote.
The remote will be sold on an international scale.
The industrial designer reported on working design, explaining how a remote control works and describing its main components.
The marketing expert will work on trend watching
The remote will have a simple, trendy design, with some kind of special feature that makes it stand out.

It was decided that the remote would feature an LCD screen, rubber buttons, colorful rubber changeable skins, a kinetic battery, and possibly speech recognition if it is still within the budget to include it.
The marketing expert also stated that young users like speech recognition and that users in general want buttons for power, channel selection, volume control, and a few lesser used settings.
The production costs cannot exceed 12.50 Euro.
The industrial designer will work on the working design of the remote.
Whether the remote will be used exclusively for televisions.
He stressed that a trendy design is important, that users zap a lot, and that remotes often get lost.
They were not sure how much a recharger would cost to make.
The industrial designer will focus on the components concept.
The marketing expert, industrial designer and user interface designer will have thirty minutes after lunch to work on their individual presentations.
The team will not work with teletext.
He suggested substituting a kinetic battery for the rechargeable batteries and using a combination of rubber and plastic for the materials.

The project manager introduced the upcoming project to the team members and then the team members participated in an exercise in which they drew their favorite animal and discussed what they liked about the animal.

It was decided that a kinetic battery would be used in place of a rechargeable battery, that the remote will feature an LCD screen and rubber casing and rubber buttons, and that interchangeable rubber covers in fruit colors will be available.
He announced that speech recognition was still an option to consider, depending on price.
He suggested that a trendy design should not have many buttons.
The group also discussed making the remote a rounded, ergonomic shape, and using flashing lights to help locate it when lost.

The marketing expert discussed the findings of a survey which indicated that current remotes are ugly, difficult to use, have a number of unused buttons, frustrate users when misplaced, and contribute to RSI.
The Industrial Designer presented all the components of the device and announced that several of the features already discussed would not be available.
Even though the new project requirements stated that teletext was outdated, the group felt they should still include one teletext button.
The project manager opened the meeting.
The group were still unsure whether to include some DVD/VCR functions on the remote.
Speech recognition may be included if it is not too costly.
The remote will sell for 25 Euro.
Allowing users in the same household to have their own remotes with personal settings.

The user interface designer presented existing remotes to exemplify the need for simpler designs, discussed the use of components such as titanium and a back-lit LCD screen, and discussed other features to consider such as color options.

The group discussed what functions and features the remote should have, and whether to include DVD/VCR controls, a teletext button, stop button, changeable covers, and a base/recharger with locator function.
The marketing executive will work on what requirements the remote has to fulfill
The remote is only for TV, should not include a teletext feature, and should feature the company colour and slogan.
Making the remote universal.
The Marketing Expert made a presentation on trend watching, including trends in user requirements and trends in fashion.
The group had difficulty deciding what special feature they should include to make their product stand out.
The Project Manager reviewed the decisions from the previous meeting.
The user interface designer will focus on the user interface concept.
Users habits in jumping from channel to channel.
The marketing expert reported on user requirements, including how users rated the importance of different features.
How speech recognition commands work.
An automatic on/off feature will not be used.
After the project manager's closing, the project manager recapped some decisions and the team discussed how to handle the issue of locating a remote when misplaced.
The project manager talked about the project finances and selling prices.
The project manager will write up the minutes, and put the minutes from both this meeting and the previous one in the project folder.

The User Interface Designer presented his main interface design, which included buttons for the most frequently used features and a graphic user interface on the LCD screen for other functions, to keep frequently used features easy to use.
The user interface designer talked about what functions should be included.
If the budget allows it the remote will include a base unit with a locator function, which will also act as a recharger.
The industrial designer discussed the interior workings of a remote and how to handle universal capability and speech recognition.
The team will concentrate on making a remote only for televisions and then make their product more generalized later.
The project manager informed the group of new requirements.
How to locate a remote when misplaced.
The basic functions should include an on/off switch, buttons for channels one to nine, volume, mute and buttons for next and previous channel.
